name: Transaction Classification
description: SHIPPED BASELINE. CLASSIFY 0.3.3 is production-usable as a local deterministic owner-rulebook classifier. The released Native-AOT CLI publishes twelve classify.* operations for rule lifecycle, evaluation, single-outcome explanation, explicit preview/apply, feedback, status, abandonment, and cleanup. The final module gate passed 5,609 tests. Owner validation over 617 eligible transactions produced 146 suggestions and 471 no-suggestions with zero conflicts, stale results, or drift canaries and identical replay evidence; the active 14-rule set retains broadApplyAllowed=false and no Ledger category mutations were made by that evaluation-only validation. Ledger classification_v1 and mutation preconditions are released public dependencies. Historical automatic-discovery failure and its kill criteria remain preserved; they do not describe the shipped owner-authored rulebook path.

INCREMENT PROBLEM. Real operator use exposed throughput and discoverability friction, not classifier-engine correctness defects: obtaining 146 selectable outcomes through one classify.outcome.get process per transaction exceeded a five-minute orchestration timeout; active rule-set and rule-version discovery are indirect; constructing a correctly bound private validation corpus is manual and error-prone; and repeated no_suggestion patterns cannot be reviewed as a bounded owner-local report.

APPROACH A — EXPLICIT ERGONOMICS QUERIES AND ONE SAFE LOCAL BUILDER (selected). Add paginated outcome and rule discovery, an explicit active-rule-set summary, a bounded unresolved-pattern report, and an idempotent owner-only corpus builder. Compose bulk preview from returned outcome IDs and the unchanged selected_outcomes contract. Complexity M. Pros: preserves explicit authority, typed operations, deterministic pagination, existing Ledger truth, and the no-implicit-apply boundary. Cons: adds five public operations and cursor/storage query code.

APPROACH B — GENERIC SEARCH/REPORT ACTION. Add one generic classify.query operation with discriminator-shaped filters and outputs. Complexity M. Rejected because it weakens schema discovery, source-generated JSON precision, typed errors, stable operation ownership, and independent limits.

APPROACH C — DO LESS IN THE ORCHESTRATOR. Keep the twelve-operation surface and script one classify.outcome.get process per row while hand-authoring corpora. Complexity L. Rejected because measured operator use already exceeded the five-minute orchestration window and the workaround duplicates privacy-sensitive binding logic outside Tally.

BOUNDARIES. The core engine, grammar, rule authority, apply saga, feedback semantics, and broadApplyAllowed=false policy remain unchanged. No autonomous merchant intelligence, automatic rule creation or activation, background worker, cloud/ML/fuzzy/regex behavior, private raw-description store, or apply-everything shortcut is introduced. Owner-visible descriptions may appear only in the bounded unresolved report result and private corpus file; they never enter logs, graph, tracked docs, cursor payloads, durable report state, or general discovery operations. This increment stays inside CLASSIFY as a new post-release plan rather than a new module.
problem_statement: CLASSIFY is shipped and correct, but an owner or Hermes agent cannot efficiently discover evaluation outcomes, inspect the active rulebook, assemble a fresh private validation corpus, or review repeated unresolved descriptions through bounded public operations. The concrete regression is that enumerating 146 outcomes with one classify.outcome.get process per row exceeded a five-minute orchestration timeout. The missing product capability is operator throughput and discoverability while preserving explicit selection, owner-only privacy, Ledger authority, and fail-closed mutation.
why_now: The 0.3.3 rulebook is active in evaluation-only mode and has been exercised against the real Ledger. Its 23.66 percent safe suggestion coverage is usable, but the current one-row discovery path makes routine review and rulebook refinement too slow and brittle. The next release should improve operator composition before expanding rule authority or classifier intelligence.

rationale: Classification evaluates and updates canonical ledger transactions and spend-category assignments.
